chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The rider should give salam to the walker, and the standing one to the seated one.

key_terms.الرَّاكِبُ: the rider, one mounted on an animal (or in some later scholarly interpretations, a vehicle)
key_terms.يُسَلِّمُ: gives salam, initiates the greeting — from سَلَّمَ (to greet with peace)

ai.seo_question: Who should initiate the salam greeting according to Imam al-Sadiq: the rider or the walker?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes an etiquette rule for initiating the Islamic greeting (salam): the one on a higher or more commanding position — the rider, the one in motion above — defers to the less prominent by greeting first. This ruling reflects the Islamic principle that humility and courtesy should accompany social encounters, with the salam serving as a bond of brotherhood. The original audience would have applied this literally to horse/camel riders greeting those on foot, and to those standing approaching the seated.
